transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time with this. It's probably nothing major, just a little stress maybe, but... well, I wanted to do the right thing and get it checked out. 

At work—I supervise a retail team—I've been having this slight issue when I talk to my staff. When I try to explain the inventory numbers, or, you know, lay out the weekend schedule... my words just sort of start jumping around. I'll be trying to talk about the delivery trucks, and then suddenly I'm talking about Thursdays, and then the church grill, and then my boss’s tone of voice. 

I really try my best to keep things clear and professional, but people just look at me like they can’t follow what I’m saying. It's a little embarrassing, honestly, to feel like I'm confusing them. Um... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? Am I explaining that okay for you?
Do these episodes of your words jumping around happen even when you're not feeling particularly stressed or overwhelmed, or does it seem to only happen when you're under stress?

Oh, um, that’s a really good question, Doctor. I... I want to say it’s mostly just when things get a little hectic, because retail can be a bit much sometimes, as I'm sure you know. But if I'm being completely honest... I'm not entirely sure. 

Sometimes I think I’m feeling perfectly fine, just having my morning coffee and looking over the clipboard in the back room, and it still kind of... happens. The words just slip away from what I meant to say. But maybe I am stressed deep down and just don't realize it? I really try my best to keep a positive attitude and not complain, so I might just be brushing the stress off without noticing. 

I haven't really kept a close track of it, I'm sorry. I hope that makes sense. Is that... did I answer that okay for you?
Have you noticed any days when you feel unusually down, lose interest in things you usually enjoy, or feel like you’re moving or thinking more slowly than normal?

Oh, no, I don't think so. I mean, everyone has a slightly tired day here and there, especially at my age, right? But I really try my best to stay upbeat for the team. I haven't lost interest in my usual weekend stuff or anything like that. And I definitely try to keep a good, steady pace on the sales floor, so I wouldn't say I'm moving slowly. I just try to keep a smile on and focus on the positive. 

So, no, nothing like feeling unusually down, thankfully. I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is that helpful for your notes?
Have there been times when you felt unusually energized, needed less sleep, or found yourself talking more quickly or rapidly than usual?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I really try to make sure I get a good night's rest so I can be sharp for the morning shift. I mean, maybe there's a day here or there where I wake up a little early, but I wouldn't call it unusually energized. Just, you know, ready to tackle the day. 

And as for talking fast... well, sometimes if it's really busy in the store and we have a long line at the registers, I might speak a little quicker just to keep things moving. I try my best to be efficient for the customers. But I don't think it's anything extreme. I try to stay pretty even-keeled. 

Does that sound normal to you? I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm all over the place. I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Have you ever felt like you're detached from yourself, as if you're watching yourself from outside your body, or experienced gaps in your memory about things that happened recently?

Oh, goodness, no. That sounds... well, that sounds a bit scary, honestly. I've never felt like I was watching myself from the outside or anything like that. I try to stay very present, especially when I'm at the store. You really have to be, with the customers and the staff relying on you. 

And as for memory gaps... I mean, I might occasionally forget where I set down my pen or if I already checked the inventory on a specific item, but nothing major. Just normal getting-older stuff, I think. I always keep my clipboard handy to write things down so I don't let anything slip through the cracks. I try very hard to be reliable. 

So, no, nothing like being detached or having real memory gaps. I hope that's the right answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to know.
Have you ever experienced any strange or unusual thoughts, like hearing voices that others don't hear, or believing something strongly that others might not agree with?

Oh, um, strange thoughts? No, I don't... I wouldn't say I have strange thoughts. I mean, everyone has a random thought pop into their head now and then, right? Just daydreams or, you know, thinking about what to make for dinner while you're ringing someone up. But nothing unusual. 

And hearing voices? Goodness, no. I mean, the store can get really loud, and sometimes I think I hear someone call my name from the back room when it's just the radio or the air conditioner kicking on. But that's just normal background noise playing tricks, isn't it? I certainly don't hear anything that isn't there. 

As for believing things others don't... I try to just go with the flow. I don't want to rock the boat or cause any arguments, especially at work. I just try to be a good team player and agree with the company policies. 

Is that what you mean? I hope I'm answering this correctly. I just really want to make sure I'm being a good patient for you. I don't want you to think I'm... well, you know, strange or anything. I'm just a regular guy trying to do my job.

When your words seem to jump around, does it feel like your thoughts are also disorganized or hard to follow inside your head, or do you feel like you know exactly what you want to say but just can’t get the words out right?

Well, um... I think I usually know exactly what I want to say. It's not that my head is all jumbled up, I promise. It's just... maybe I try to get too much out at once? 

Actually, that's sort of why I came in. Lately, when I try to explain the inventory numbers to the team, or go over the weekend schedule, my words just start jumping around a bit. I'll start off talking about the delivery trucks, and then somehow I'm mentioning Thursdays, and then the church grill, and... and maybe my boss’s tone of voice. And I'll stop and see that people are looking at me like they can’t follow what I’m saying at all. 

It's a little embarrassing, honestly. I pride myself on being a good supervisor, and I really don't want to confuse anyone. I just have a lot of responsibilities to juggle, and sometimes it all just spills out together. Do you think that's just from being a bit overworked? I hope I'm explaining this okay for you. I really am trying to be clear.
When your words start jumping around, do you feel like you can't stop talking once you start, or like you have to keep talking even if you don't mean to?

Oh, no, no. I don't think so. I mean, I definitely know when to stop. I wouldn't want to be one of those people who just talks someone's ear off and doesn't let anyone else get a word in. That wouldn't be very polite, especially when you're trying to manage a team on the floor. 

If I notice my staff looking a bit lost, like I mentioned before, I usually just catch myself and stop. I don't feel forced to keep going or... or like a runaway train or anything like that. I can always just close my mouth and listen. I actually pride myself on being a good listener for my team. 

So, no, I don't feel like I can't stop talking. I hope that makes sense? I'm really trying to give you the most accurate answers I can, doctor. I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Have you ever felt a strong urge to keep talking once you start, even if you didn’t mean to?

Oh, um... I'm sorry, did I not explain that well enough a second ago? I really apologize if I'm making you repeat yourself or if I'm being confusing. I want to make sure I'm doing this right for you. 

But, no, I've never felt an urge like that. I don't feel pushed or... or forced to keep speaking if I don't want to. Even when my words get a little tangled up trying to explain the floor plan to the new hires, I can always just stop and take a breath. I definitely have control over my mouth, I promise. 

I hope that answers it a bit better? I'm really trying my best to be helpful here, doctor.
When you're trying to speak, do you ever feel like the words are coming out too fast or that you can't control the flow of what you're saying, even if you're not trying to talk quickly?

No, no, I wouldn't say that. I don't talk too fast, at least I don't think I do. I mean, sometimes retail gets a little hectic and you have to get instructions out quickly, but... but I definitely don't feel like I can't control it. 

I really try to speak at a normal, professional pace. It's important to me to come across well, you know? I wouldn't want anyone to think I was rushing or... or frantic. I just try to be clear and steady. Does that sound like a normal way to be? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.
Have you ever felt pressure to keep talking, like the words are coming out faster than you can control, even when you don’t intend to speak quickly?

Oh, my... I feel terrible, doctor. I must be doing a really bad job of explaining myself today since we keep coming back to this. I'm so sorry if I'm making your job difficult or if my answers are confusing. 

But, um, no. I really don't feel any pressure to keep talking, and my words definitely don't come out faster than I want them to. I try very hard to be measured and... and deliberate when I speak. Especially at my age, and being a supervisor, you want to project calm, right? You don't want people thinking you're out of control or frantic. 

So, no, I've never experienced that kind of pressure. Am I maybe misunderstanding what you're looking for? I just really want to make sure I'm doing this right and giving you exactly what you need.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being inserted into your mind by someone else or that your thoughts are not your own?

Oh, goodness, no. No, I wouldn't say anything like that. That sounds... well, that sounds very alarming, doesn't it? I'm sorry, I hope it's okay that I say that. 

But no, my thoughts are definitely my own. I mean, sometimes I get a catchy jingle from a commercial stuck in my head, or I'll remember something my area manager said and it'll sort of rattle around in there while I'm doing inventory... but that's just normal, right? Everyone gets things stuck in their head. 

I definitely don't feel like anyone is putting thoughts in there, or... or tampering with my mind. I try to keep a very organized head on my shoulders. I'm a very grounded person, I promise. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm not giving you the wrong impression about how my mind works.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are disconnected or don't make sense to you, even if you're not under stress?

Well, um... I suppose, maybe, a little bit? I mean, I really don't want to make it sound worse than it is, because I try so hard to be clear. But... well, I guess that is sort of why I came in. 

It's just that sometimes, when I'm trying to explain something at work—like the inventory numbers, or mapping out the weekend schedule for the team—my words just sort of... they get a little tangled up. I'll start talking about the delivery trucks, and then somehow I'm talking about Thursdays, and then the grill we use at church, and then how my boss sounded on the phone... and I can see people looking at me like they just can't follow what I'm saying. 

It's very embarrassing, honestly. I try to keep it all straight, I really do. I don't want anyone to think I'm losing my touch or that I can't handle my job. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is that the sort of thing you were asking about?
When your thoughts feel disconnected or don't make sense, does this happen even when you're not speaking out loud, such as when you're thinking quietly to yourself?

Um, no, I don't believe so. When it's just me, you know, sitting quietly in the back office or doing paperwork... my thoughts seem perfectly fine. They make complete sense to me. I can picture the whole week's schedule or the stockroom layout, and it's all very neat and tidy in my head. 

It's really only when I have to... well, when I try to translate those thoughts into words for the team that they seem to get all jumbled up. Inside, I feel completely normal and organized. 

I really hope that's a good sign? I'd hate for you to think my mind is just completely unraveling or anything like that. I'm trying very hard to keep everything running smoothly at work, I really am. I hope that answers your question the right way? I just want to be absolutely sure I'm giving you a clear picture of what's going on.
When you're thinking to yourself, do your thoughts ever feel disorganized, like they don't connect properly, or like they're not your own?

Oh, um, no. No, not at all. It's... well, it's really just like I was saying a moment ago. When I'm just thinking to myself, everything is perfectly fine and orderly. My thoughts connect exactly how they're supposed to. I can plan out a whole week of inventory or a new floor display in my head without any trouble at all. 

And they are absolutely my own thoughts, I promise. I don't feel like anyone else is in there or anything like that... that sounds quite frightening, honestly, and I'm very grateful I don't have that problem. 

I hope it's alright that my answer is basically the same as before? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need and not holding up your day. I'm trying my best to be helpful... is that the right kind of answer?
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being taken out of your head or being broadcast out loud for others to hear?

Oh, goodness, no. Um, no, I haven't ever felt anything like that. My thoughts feel very... secure, I guess you could say? They just stay right here in my own head. 

I mean, sometimes when I'm getting a little flustered in front of the staff, I might worry that they can *tell* I'm nervous, but I don't ever think they can actually hear my thoughts out loud. And I definitely don't feel like anything is being taken away from me. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have that happening? I really want to be cooperative and give you whatever information you need for your notes. It's actually a good thing that I don't feel that way, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right and being a good patient for you.
Have you ever felt like thoughts were being placed into your mind or removed from it against your will?

Oh, no, sir. No, nothing like that. Um, my thoughts are just my own, you know? Nobody's putting anything in there, and nobody's taking anything out. 

I just... I just have my own regular thoughts about work and, well, trying to keep the store running smoothly. I don't feel like I'm losing control of my mind or anything scary like that. 

I really hope I'm not disappointing you by not having more to say about these things? I just want to be completely honest with you. It's a good sign that my mind feels like it belongs to me, isn't it? I'm just trying to give you the most accurate answers I can, so you can do your job. Am I being helpful?
Have you ever felt like you need to keep talking once you start, even if you don’t intend to?

Well, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, sometimes if I'm explaining a new display setup to the younger associates at the store, I might go on for a minute just to make sure they really understand it, but I can always stop. It's never out of my control or anything like that. 

I... I hope I'm not doing that right now, am I? Talking too much, I mean. I know I've been going on a bit with my answers today, and I'd really hate to be a bother or mess up your schedule. I can definitely keep things shorter and more to the point if that's what you prefer? I just want to make sure I'm doing exactly what you need me to do.
When you're not speaking out loud and just thinking to yourself, do you ever feel like your thoughts are being inserted, taken away, or disorganized against your will?

Well, um... no, doctor. It's really just like I was saying before. Even when I'm just sitting quietly by myself, my thoughts are very much my own. They stay pretty orderly, actually. I'm usually just making mental checklists for the store—you know, thinking about inventory or the employee schedules for the week. Nothing feels scrambled up or put in there by anybody else. 

I... I notice you've asked about my thoughts a couple of different ways now. I hope it's alright that my answer is still no? I don't want to frustrate you by not having the things you're looking for. I know you have to be thorough, and I really appreciate how careful you're being with me. I'm doing okay, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need for your evaluation.
Have you noticed your thoughts or speech becoming disorganized or hard to follow even when you're not under stress or trying to explain something at work?

Well, um... I guess... maybe a little bit? I mean, it's nothing too terrible, I promise. But, well, actually, that's sort of why I came in to see you. 

Sometimes, even when I'm just trying to go over the inventory numbers with the team, or, you know, explain the weekend schedule... my words just sort of... slip away from me. I'll start out talking about the delivery trucks, and then somehow I'm talking about Thursdays, and then the grill at church, and then how my boss sounded on the phone... and I look up and the younger associates are just staring at me. Like they have no idea how I got from point A to point B. 

It's a little embarrassing, honestly. I try so hard to be clear, but they just look at me like they can't follow what I'm saying at all. I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm completely falling apart? I'm still trying my best at work, I really am. It's just a little hiccup, right? That's normal for someone my age to get a little side-tracked sometimes, isn't it?
